portable

Portable is a modern PDF graphics device for R, created to supplement the ragg and svglite graphics devices. As such, it is built on the same foundation, using the systemfonts and textshaping font stack. In contrast to svglite, the purpose of portable outputs is to be, well, portable. As such it embeds fonts natively ensuring that the graphics is presented equivalently on any system.

Like it’s graphics device cousins it intends to keep up to date with new capabilities in the R graphics engine to the extent that the PDF specs allow it. As an example:

  • It supports Porter-Duff blending operations even though these are not present in the PDF spec because they can be recreated by various combinations of alpha blending (except "add" and "saturate"). The grDevices::pdf() device achieves this through rasterization which is counter to the purpose of PDF.
  • It does not support device capture because it is not a rasterizing device.

Installation

You can install the development version of portable like so:

pak::pak("r-lib/portable")

Example

portable exports a single function portable_pdf() which works like pdf() and opens a graphics device to plot to:

library(portable)
temp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
portable_pdf(temp_file)
plot(1:10, 1:10)
dev.off()
#> quartz_off_screen 
#>                 2

file.size(temp_file)
#> [1] 4047
